title: Video courses for 300,000 students
summary: CursosMX sells recorded courses to 300,000 students in Mexico and Central America. Videos must arrive fast, raw recordings must cost little, and the login receives SQL injection attempts.

requirements.1: {{s1}} keeps copies of videos and images at points close to each student, so requests do not travel to the region every time.
requirements.2: {{s2}} is the origin of millions of videos that students watch every day over HTTP, in a single region; you pay per stored GB and there are no servers to manage.
requirements.3: {{s3}} keeps the raw recordings for 5 years, and they are almost never opened. What matters is the lowest cost per stored GB the region offers, even if reading them later costs more.
requirements.4: {{s4}} holds the records for cursosmx.com and answers anyone on the internet who asks for that name, so they reach slot 1.
requirements.5: {{s5}} checks every HTTP request to the login and blocks SQL injection before it reaches the app.
requirements.6: The app load balancer spreads login and payments across the servers in the region.

s1.explanation: Azure Front Door is a CDN on the Microsoft edge network, with points of presence close to users, and it caches content. Traffic Manager only answers through DNS and does not see the traffic.

s2.explanation: Blob Storage stores massive amounts of unstructured data, is designed for streaming video and is read over HTTP or HTTPS from anywhere. The hot tier is for data accessed frequently.

s3.explanation: Mexico Central offers the hot, cool and cold tiers of Blob Storage, but not archive. Of those three, cold has the lowest cost per GB; it has a 90-day minimum and charges more per read, although it answers in milliseconds.
s3.hint_cue: the lowest cost per stored GB

s4.explanation: Azure Public DNS hosts domains such as cursosmx.com and their records so the internet can resolve them. Azure Private DNS only resolves names inside virtual networks.

s5.explanation: The Application Gateway WAF protects against SQL injection; its policy is associated with the Application Gateway and blocks the request without forwarding it to the back end. DDoS Protection covers layers 3 and 4.

azure-traffic-manager.s1: Traffic Manager works at the DNS level: the student connects directly to the chosen endpoint, and Traffic Manager is not a proxy and does not see the traffic, so it keeps no copies.
azure-traffic-manager.s4: Traffic Manager only picks an endpoint; the records for cursosmx.com live in the service that hosts the domain, which points to it with a CNAME.

azure-managed-disks.s2: A managed disk is a block storage volume used with Azure virtual machines; the video origin must serve over HTTP with no servers to manage.
azure-managed-disks.s3: A managed disk is a block storage volume for virtual machines, not one of the Blob Storage access tiers.

azure-blob-cool.s3: The cool tier costs less per GB than hot, but more than cold; Microsoft places it for data read rarely and cold for data almost never read.
azure-blob-cool.s2: The cool tier is for data that is rarely read or changed and charges for every GB read; the videos are watched every day.

azure-private-dns.s4: Azure Private DNS manages and resolves names inside the virtual network; students on the internet do not get its answers.

azure-ddos-protection.s5: DDoS Protection works at layers 3 and 4; protecting a web application at layer 7 needs another piece.
